 Mr. Raj B  CORAM:
HON'BLE DR.JUSTICE SANJEEB K PANIGRAHI  ORDER 30.03.2026 Order No.
1 . This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement.

2. In filing this I.A. under Section 430(1) of B.N.S.S., the Appellant being in custody pursuant to the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 18.11.2024 passed by the learned Ad-hoc Addl. Sessions Judge (FTSC), POCSO, Rourkela in S.T. Case No.81/39 of 2017-2023, has prayed for releasing him on bail.

3. Heard learned counsel for the Appellant and learned counsel for the State.
4. As per the order dated 14.07.2025, learned counsel for the Designation: Senior Stenographer Reason: Authentication Location: HIGH COURT OF State has produced the custody certificate of the Appellant ORISSA, CUTTACK Date: 31-Mar-2026 19:20:14 from the Superintendent,
Special-Jail, Rourkela which indicates that the Appellant has remained in judicial custody for more than 3 years.
The custody certificate is taken on record.

5. Learned counsel for the Appellant submits that the Appellant has been convicted and sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of two years and to pay a fine of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand)
only to the victim girl, in default, to undergo R.I. for a further period of six months for the offence under Section 354 of the I.P.C. and he further sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- (rupees one lakh) only to the victim girl, on default, to undergo R.I.

sentences.text: She further contends that the Appellant has remained in judicial custody for more than three years and since there is no chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future, the bail application of the Appellant be favourably considered.
6. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, supported the impugned judgment and opposes the prayer for bail.

7. Considering the submissions made on behalf of the learned counsel for the respective parties, the available materials on record, particularly the nature of evidence adduced during trial, while not inclining to release the Appellant on bail on merit but taking into account the period of detention of the Appellant in judicial custody and absence of early hearing of the appeal in the near future, this Court is of the view that the Appellant should be enlarged on interim bail for a period of two months.

This Court, accordingly, directs that the Appellant shall be released on interim bail for a period of two months from the date of his actual release from the custody in connection with the above noted case by the learned Court in seisin over the matter on such terms and conditions as deemed just and proper with further conditions that he will positively surrender before the learned Court in seisin over the matter on the date as would be so directed.
The Appellant is also directed not to threaten the victim or her family members in any manner.
8. This I.A. is, accordingly, disposed of.

9. List this matter on 29th June, 2026 for final hearing.
10.

The Registry is directed to prepare the paper book in the meantime and supply the same to the learned counsel for the Appellant so also learned counsel for the State in accordance with Orissa High Court Rules.
11. Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
12. Both the parties are directed to file their respective written notes of submissions on or before the next date of listing of this matter.

(Dr. Sanjeeb K Panigrahi) Judge Sipun Pankaja Muna @ vs State Of Odisha on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37510813/
